Keypad codes: original / v25 values. New games in v26+ shuffle them. Airlock: always 9831.
Access levels (each includes all preceding levels): 0 — [5F];1 — +[4F];2 — +[G];3 — +[L1, L2];4 — +[L7, L8];5 — +[2F, L5];6 — +[3F, L4, L6];7 — +[1F, L3]. Parking and Warehouse have separate entrances.

Reading the map

S — respawn cell $0E. ● is an initial enemy from a separate table; these positions do not coincide with S. Enemy sprites face the viewer and use the selected floor's normal palette. Pickups use their inventory icons. Doors are shown from six cells away; the alarm tile from three. R on L4 marks rescue with a Bomb. The Visor 1 preview shows three adjacent beam cells from eight cells away, with the camera raised for a jump. Interaction panels appear beside objects: the terminal after inserting the card, and Screen images after loading the recording. Lighting and gas are floor states, not separate map cells.

Original game credits

This atlas uses maps, graphics, sprites and palettes from the original game Corporation / Cyber-Cop, for Sega Mega Drive / Genesis (1992). Scene previews were produced by its renderer.

Development: Core Design Ltd.
Design and graphics: Kevin Bulmer.
Programming: William Allen.
Music and sound effects: Krisalis Software Ltd.
Production and copyright as credited in the game: Virgin Games Inc.

Project manager: Lyle J. Hall II.
Quality assurance: Lyle J. Hall II, Tom Tallarico, Michael Gater, Ron Friedman, Noah Tool.
Manual: Lyle J. Hall II; editor — Lisa Marcinko.

Names are taken from the Genesis end credits. Rights to the original game and its assets belong to their respective rights holders. Historical credits do not establish current ownership. This unofficial atlas is not affiliated with the original publishers or developers.
